dedupe_keys.name: peartree convert gtfs schedules into directed network graphs

description: peartree is a Python library that converts GTFS feed schedules into a representative directed network graph. The README says it uses the Partridge library to read the target operator's schedule, identifies the busiest day as a representative feed and builds a NetworkX graph for a chosen time period; its example loads several San Francisco Bay Area operators incrementally and converts an AC Transit feed. It installs from PyPI and was written by Kuan Butts. Coverage: any GTFS feed. Format and access: an open-source Python package. Licence and cost: MIT, free. Caveats: the README badges point to Travis CI and Gitter, which suggests an older project, and the graph is a schedule summary, not a full timetable model. It supports network flow and cascading failure studies that remove stops or links from a transit graph. It relates to OSMnx, City2Graph and the GTFS specification in the catalogue.
